Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:177821
Court No. - 75

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 30709 of 2024
Applicant :- Gyanendra Prasad Shukla @ Bauwa

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Manvendra Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Syed Mohammed Jafer Husain
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Second Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

3. The present third bail application has been filed by the applicant involved in case crime No. 122 of 2022, under Sections 363, 302, 201, 376-Ka, 376-Ka (Kha) IPC, Section 5(i)/5(e)/6 of POCSO Act and Section 3(2)5 of SC/ST Act, police station Kalyanpur, District Fatehpur with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

The first bail application of applicant was rejected by this Court vide order Gyanendra Prasad Shukla @ Bauwa vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98524402/
1 dated 7.4.2023, passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.4023 of 2023.

sentences.text:
4. The second bail application of the applicant was rejected vide order dated 16.02.2024, which is reproduced as below:-
"1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant-accused, learned counsel for the first informant, Ms. Gunajn Sharma, learned counsel for High Court Legal Services Authority and learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

2. The present second bail application has been filed by the applicant involved in case crime No. 122 of 2022, under Sections 363, 302, 201, 376-Ka, 376-Ka (Kha) IPC,
Section 5(i)/5(e)/6 of POCSO Act and Section 3(2)5 of SC/ST Act, police station Kalyanpur, District Fatehpur with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

The first bail application of applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 7.4.2023, passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.4023 of 2023.
3.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.4023 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It was submitted that applicant is not named in the first information report, which was lodged by the informant against unknown persons, alleging that on 12.07.2022 his daughter, aged about 6 years, has gone to school but thereafter she has gone missing.
Learned senior counsel submitted that there is no eye witness of alleged incident.

After five days of incident, the statements of alleged witnesses, namely, Brijendra Kumar Paswan and Shivbali Paswan were recorded and they have inter alia stated that on 17.07.2022 they have seen that applicant was present at the hand pump in front of the closet (Kothari) and that deceased was plucking the black-currants (Karaunda) near that place.
It was further submitted that long delay of five days in recording their statements creates serious doubt about the authenticity of their version.
5. It is further submitted that first bail application of applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 7.4.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.4023 of 2023.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.4023 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The main ground taken in this second bail application is that after rejection of first bail application, the prosecution has got discharged several independent witnesses, who claimed to have seen the deceased with applicant and thus, now the prosecution version regarding alleged 'last seen' evidence becomes doubtful.

It was pointed out that while rejecting the first bail application of the applicant, the court has taken into consideration the statements of alleged independent witnesses who have got dropped by the prosecution.

It has been submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail since 17.07.2022, having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in trial.

4. Learned counsel for the informant, learned counsel for High Court Legal Services Authority and learned AGA have opposed the prayer for bail and argued that said witnesses were discharged by the prosecution as they have been win over by the applicant.

It was pointed out that there were other witnesses, who have seen the deceased with applicant and thus, the discharge of said witnesses Gyanendra Prasad Shukla @ Bauwa vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98524402/
2 would be of no consequence.

entities.text: Gyanendra Prasad Shukla @ Bauwa vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case relates to molestation and murder of a six years old girl.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, gravity of offence and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, the applicant is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the second bail application of applicant is hereby rejected.

6. However, keeping in view of period of incarceration of applicant, the trial court is directed to expedite the trial and to decide the same preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of copy of this order, if there is no legal impediment."
5.
It is submitted by learned counsel for applicant that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
There is no eye witness of the aforesaid case.
During trial, statements of three witnesses of fact as well as of other formal witnesses have been recorded before the trial Court.
Certain witnesses, who were examined during investigation, have been dropped by the prosecution during trial.
There is no possibility of tampering with evidence.
There are contradictions in the statement of witnesses.
Criminal history of applicant has been explained.

While rejecting second bail application of the applicant, the trial Court was directed to expedite the trial and to decide the same preferably within a period of six months but the trial has not been decided so far.
It was submitted that applicant is in jail since 17.07.2022 and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.

6. Learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. have opposed the bail application and submitted that the deceased was a minor girl aged about six years and while she was going to school,
she was molested and brutally murdered.
The deceased was last seen with applicant accused.
There are serious allegations against the applicant.
7. The case relates to molestation and murder of six years old girl.
Deceased was seen with applicant.
It appears that most of the witnesses have been examined before the trial Court and the trial is at the advanced stage.
8. Considering the entire facts, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Hence, the third bail application of applicant is hereby rejected.

9. However, the Trial Court is again directed to expedite the trial and to conclude the same as early as possible preferably within a period of six months from the date of production of copy of this order.
10. A copy of this order be transmitted to the concerned trial court for necessary compliance.

Order Date :- 12.11.2024 RKM  Gyanendra Prasad Shukla @ Bauwa vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98524402/
